sentences.show: In 1590, a governor came back to his colony in America. Everyone was gone. The only clue was one word, carved into a post.
The Roanoke Colony, sent by Sir Walter Raleigh.
In 1587, about 115 men, women and children landed on Roanoke Island.
Weeks later, the governor's granddaughter was born. Virginia Dare, the first English child born in the New World.
The colonists sent the governor, John White, back to England for supplies.
Then the Spanish Armada came. Every English ship was kept at home.
It took White three years to get back. He landed on his granddaughter's third birthday.
The houses were taken apart. His chests were dug up and looted. The boats were gone. And every single person.
They had agreed. If you leave, carve where you went. If you're in danger, carve a cross. There was no cross. Just CROATOAN.
Croatoan was a nearby island of friendly natives. But a storm snapped the anchor cable, and White had to sail away.
He never saw his family again.
Today, on Hatteras Island, the old Croatoan, archaeologists have found English sword and gun parts in a Native village.
Did they simply join the tribe? Or did that word mean something else? Where did they go?
Croatoan was their clue. Subscribe is yours.
